model.name: DREAM S2 semantic news-cycle retention
model.lambda_interpretation: lambda = elapsed hours since semantic topic attention peak
model.abstraction_layer: Raw RSS articles are converted into stable semantic topic objects before S2 fitting.
model.semantic_layer: Sparse TF-IDF article vectors, entity sets, keyword distributions, semantic connected components, centroid inertia, and a persistent topic_memory.json file.
model.event_horizon_layer: H(t)=Deviation(t)*CrossScaleCoherence(t), with Deviation=observed/expected_S2 and CrossScaleCoherence from source-tier spread, source diversity, and semantic coherence. Pre-horizon alerts require high H and positive slope.
model.signal_preprocessing: Formal S2 fit uses circadian-corrected publish-time article counts: raw count divided by expected global publishing/activity factor.
model.observation_clock: article.published_at, not GitHub Action run time
model.history_role: data/history.json retains raw article records and first_seen/last_seen provenance; topic_memory.json retains semantic identity; cycles.json retains completed S2 cycle summaries.
model.comparison: Delta AIC = AIC(exponential beta=1) - AIC(stretched S2 beta free)
model.cycle_archive_role: data/cycles.json stores deduplicated completed formal cycle summaries so prior S2 learning remains visible when a new wave resets the current topic. Current waves are not archived until replaced by a new peak.

articles.summary: Sagal Abdi-Wali, who came from Somalia in 1990s, will likely face Zack Polanski in Holborn and St Pancras contest A former child refugee who became the leader of Camden council has been selected to be the Labour candidate for the byelection in Holborn and St Pancras. Sagal Abdi-Wali, who came to the UK from Somalia as a child in the 1990s and was elected leader of Camden council in May, was chosen to represent Labour members in the north London seat vacated by Keir Starmer. She was previously the chair of the local constituency Labour party, after first being elected as a Labour councillor in 2022. Continue reading...

articles.title: Trump officials push to exclude undocumented immigrants from US census
articles.summary: Census Bureau also considers race and ethnicity questions in overhaul that would have dramatic effect on voter maps The Trump administration on Wednesday proposed changes to the US census intended to exclude immigrants without legal status in addition to other groups, with potentially significant effects on the allocation of federal resources and drawing of districts in the US House of Representatives . In a proposed rule published in the Federal Register, the Census Bureau also announced it was considering changes to the data it collects about race and ethnicity, amid the Trump administration’s push to rid the government of diversity, equity and inclusion programs.
